title: छ माया छपक्कै २- ढोँगी समाजको मुखौटा उघार्ने चलचित्र
content:
दीपकराज गिरीको चलचित्र भन्नेवित्तिकै दिमागमा आइहाल्ने कुरा हो- हाँस्न पाइन्छ । दर्शकलाई हँसाउँदै गम्भीर सन्देश पनि दिने प्रयास गिरीले अहिलेसम्म गर्दै आएका छन् । उनको नयाँ चलचित्र ‘छ माया छपक्कै २’ अहिले दोस्रो हप्तामा चलिरहेको छ । कथा-पटकथामा विभिन्न कमजोरीका बाबजुद ‘छ माया छपक्कै २’ ले निर्मम ढङ्गबाट नेपाली समाजको ढोँगी चरित्रलाई उदाङ्गो पार्ने कोसिस गरेको छ । चलचित्रको विषयवस्तु र प्रस्तुतिमा नयाँपन छ भने केही जबरजस्त ट्वीस्टहरुले गर्दा दर्शक अन्तिमसम्म बाँधिन्छन् । चलचित्रमा मुख्य पात्र मुरलीधर (दीपकराज गिरी) पठाओ चलाउँछ । ‘छ माया छपक्कै’ को पहिलो कम्युनिस्ट बाको मार्गदर्शन पछ्याउँदै राजनीतिमा लागेको बिपी धार्मिक आमाको मार्गदर्शन पछ्याउँदै मुरलीधर बनेको छ । आफूभन्दा २० वर्ष कान्छी जल (केकी अधिकारी)सँग विवाह गरेको मुरलीधर घर गृहस्थीमा रमाउन चाहन्छ । तर, समाज बदल्छु भनेर कम्युनिस्ट भएका मुरलीधरका बाको इच्छा छोरालाई राजनीतिमा ल्याउने छ । मुरलीधरका बा तिनै हुन्, जो समाज बदल्न हिँडे तर आफ्नै घर बदल्न सकेनन् । आफू नास्तिक बनेर हिँडे, तर घर भने झनझन आस्तिक बनेर गयो । हुँदा हुँदा कम्युनिस्ट बनाउनलाई सारा ऊर्जा र विद्धता खर्च गरेको छोरा बिपी नै अन्त्यमा धार्मिक बन्यो । समाज बदल्न हिँडेको बाले घर बदल्न नसकेको फ्रस्टेसन बेलाबेला पोखिरहेका हुन्छन् । बाले मुरलीधरलाई राजनीतिमा फिर्ता ल्याउन चाहन्छन् । आफूले गर्न नसकेको सत्ताभोगको लालसा छोरामाथि थोपर्न चाहन्छन् । आफ्नो अधुरो महत्त्वाकाङ्क्षा मुरलीधरमाथि लाद्न चाहन्छन् । मुरलीधर भने राजनीतिमा फिर्ता हुन चाहँदैन । बरु साधारण र सरल जीवनयापन गरेर बाँच्न चाहन्छ । यही बिन्दुबाट चलचित्रको कथालाई अगाडि बढाइएको छ । चलचित्रको एउटा दृश्यमा मुरलीधरले बाको बाटो समातेर राजनीतिमा लाग्ने वा श्रीमतीसँग विदेश गएर सहज जीवनयापन गर्ने भन्ने विषयमा परिवारमा घनीभूत छलफल हुन्छ । यो छलफलमा बुवा एकातिर, श्रीमती जल एकातिर हुन्छन् । मुरलीधर निर्णय गर्न नसकेर बीचमा च्यापिन्छ । अलिकति पढेलेखेकी जलले आफ्नो विदेश जाने अडान स्पष्ट सँगले राख्छिन् । यसबेला बुवाले जललाई थर्काउँदै ‘महिलाले बढी बोल्न आवश्यक नरहेको’ बताउँछ । जीवनभर वामपन्थी राजनीति गरेका, लैङ्गिक समानताको वकालत गरेका बुवाले जललाई थर्काउँदै आफूभित्र निहित पितृ सत्तालाई बोमिट गरेर निकाल्छन् । मुरलीधरका बुवा जस्ता धेरै वामपन्थी नेताहरू हाम्रै अगाडि छन्, जो बाहिर महिला अधिकारका चर्का कुरा गर्छन्, घरमा महिलालाई ‘वस्तु’ को रूपमा व्यवहार गर्छन् । चलचित्रले ‘समाज बदल्छु’ भन्ने खोक्रा मानिसमाथि व्यङ्ग्य मात्र गरेको छैन, दलितहरूलाई राजनीतिका नाममा, प्रेमका नाममा कसरी प्रयोग गरिन्छ भनेर पनि देखाएको छ । हुँदाहुँदै शिक्षित भनिएका मुरलीधर र जलले समेत दलित युवतीको निरीहताको फाइदा उठाउन खोज्छन् । निर्देशक दीपेन्द्र लामा र दीपकराज गिरीले नेपाली समाजको द्वैध चरित्रलाई खोतल खातल पार्न कोसिस गरेका छन् । चलचित्र जति बलियो मुद्दा उठाएको छ, त्यसको बोझ पटकथाले बोक्न सकेको भने छैन । मुद्दा बलियो भएर मात्र चलचित्र बलियो बन्दैन, त्यो मुद्दालाई कति विश्वासनीय ढङ्गले भनिएको छ भन्ने कुराले चलचित्र बलियो हुने हो । दर्शकले चलचित्रमा घट्ने घटना र पात्रसँगै यात्रा गर्न सक्छन् कि सक्दैनन् ? राम्रो चलचित्रले यस प्रश्नको जवाफ दिन सक्नुपर्छ । चलचित्रको सुरुवाती चरणमा यति धेरै ‘क्रस कटिङ’को प्रयोग गरिएको छ कि दर्शक नै अलमलिन्छन् । आरामले, बिस्तारै, सुस्तरी दृश्यहरूको सम्पादन गरेको भए पनि हुने थियो । धेरै मुद्दाहरू पोको पारेर चलचित्र अन्धाधुन्ध दौडिएको छ । दौडने क्रममा पोको फुस्किएको छ । खासमा समयसँगै बदलिन नसकेका वामपन्थी बा, सहज जीवनयापनको खोजीमा रहेकी जल र निर्णय गर्न नसकिरहेका मुरलीधरबीचको अन्तरसङ्घर्षमा मात्र केन्द्रित भएको भए चलचित्र थप बलियो हुने थियो । जलका भाइ (रिहान गिरी) र सनिशाको अन्तरजातीय प्रेमकथाले अलग्गै समयको माग गर्छ । तर, यी दुईको प्रेमलाई यति हतारमा देखाइएको छ कि सनिशाको पीडामाथि दर्शकले संवेदना महसुस गर्नै सक्दैनन् । गर्भवती बनेकी सनिशामाथि दर्शकको सहानुभूति पलाउन नपाउँदै उनको पीडालाई निमोठिएको छ । ‘बेव सिरिज’को क्यानभासमा चलचित्रको कथा भन्न खोज्दा हुने समस्या नै यही हो । मुरलीधरको घरमा हुने पारिवारिक भोटिङको दृश्य नाटकीय छ । झनै त्यत्रा गाउँलेहरूको उपस्थितिको अर्थै थिएन । यो दृश्यका लागि व्यर्थैमा समय खर्च गरिएको छ । मुरलीधरको जँड्याहा काकाको अभिनय लाउड छ । कार्मले निर्वाह गरेको पात्रको बोलीमा नेवारी लवज प्रस्टै सुनिन्छ । यो लवजलाई अलिकति सुधार गर्न लगाएको भए हुने थियो । रवीन्द्र झाले डाक्टरको पात्र त्यति जम्न सकेका छैनन् । यद्यपि बेलाबेला उनले गर्ने कमेडीको पन्चिङ लाइनहरूले दर्शकलाई रमाइलो गराउँछ । दीपकराजको अभिनय स्वाभाविक छ । केकी र सनिशा आआफ्नो भूमिकामा जमेका छन् । केकीको पात्रलाई अलि तार्किक बनाउन सकेको भए अझैँ स्वादिलो हुने थियो । सिङ्गो जीवन नै लगाए पनि समाज बदल्न नसकेका ससुरामाथि केकीको पात्र जलले दह्रिलो तर्क राख्न सक्ने ठाउँ खाली नै थियो । जलको तर्कले ससुराले जीवनभर गर्ने राजनीतिको निर्मम समीक्षा गर्ने परिस्थितिको सृजना हुने थियो । त्यसो हुँदा समयसँगै बदलिने कि यथास्थितिमै रहने भन्ने प्रश्नको जवाफ खोज्न बा पनि बाध्य हुने थिए । चलचित्रमा सिनेम्याटोग्राफी र ब्याकग्राउण्ड सङ्गीत औसत छ । निर्देशकसँग सामाजिक मुद्दालाई हेर्ने दृष्टिकोण स्पष्ट देखिन्छ । तर, मुद्दालाई कथामा उन्ने तरीकामा थप मिहिनेत गरेको भए चलचित्र अझैँ अब्बल हुने थियो । When Deepak Raj Giri's movies are mentioned, the first thing that comes to mind is - you can laugh. Giri has been trying to give a serious message while making the audience laugh. His new movie 'Chha Maya Chhapakkai 2' is currently running in its second week. Despite various weaknesses in the story and screenplay, 'Chha Maya Chhapakkai 2' has tried to expose the hypocritical nature of Nepali society in a ruthless manner. The film's theme and presentation are new, and some powerful twists keep the audience hooked until the end. The main character in the movie, Muralidhar (Deepakraj Giri), plays Pathao. BP, who entered politics following the guidance of his first communist father in 'Chha Maya Chhapakkai', has become Muralidhar following the guidance of his religious mother. Muralidhar, who is married to Jal (Keki Adhikari), who is 20 years younger than him, wants to enjoy his home life. However, Muralidhar's father, who became a communist with the intention of changing the society, wants to bring his son into politics. Muralidhar's father is the one who set out to change society but could not change his own family. He set out as an atheist, but his family gradually became believers. His son BP, who spent all his energy and knowledge on becoming a communist, eventually became religious. Bale, who is on a journey to change society, is occasionally expressing his frustration at not being able to change his home. Bale wants to bring Muralidhar back into politics. He wants to impose his own lust for power, which he was unable to do, on his son. He wants to impose his unfulfilled ambitions on Muralidhar. Muralidhar, however, does not want to return to politics. Instead, he wants to live a simple and ordinary life. The story of the film is developed from this point. In one scene of the film, there is a heated discussion in the family about whether Muralidhar should follow his father's path and enter politics or go abroad with his wife and live a comfortable life. In this discussion, the father is on one side, and his wife Jal is on the other. Muralidhar is caught in the middle, unable to decide. Jal, who is a little educated, clearly states her stance on going abroad. At this time, the father rebukes Jal and says that 'women do not need to talk too much'. The father, who has been involved in leftist politics and advocated gender equality all his life, rebukes Jal and brings out the patriarchal power within him. We have many leftist leaders like Muralidhar's father before us, who talk loudly about women's rights outside, but treat women as 'objects' at home. The film not only satirizes the empty people who say 'I will change society', it also shows how Dalits are used in the name of politics, in the name of love. Despite being supposedly educated, Muralidhar and Jal try to take advantage of the Dalit girl's innocence. Directors Dipendra Lama and Deepak Raj Giri have tried to expose the dual nature of Nepali society. The film raises a strong issue, but the script is not able to carry its burden. A film does not become strong just because the issue is strong, it becomes strong because of how believably the issue is told. Can the audience travel with the events and characters in the film or not? A good film should be able to answer this question. So many 'cross-cutting' are used in the initial stages of the film that the audience gets confused. It would have been better if the scenes had been edited slowly, calmly, and smoothly. The film has rushed blindly, covering up many issues. The pacing has been disrupted. In fact, the film would have been stronger if it had focused solely on the internal struggle between the leftist father who has not changed with the times, Jal, who is in search of an easy life, and Muralidhar, who is unable to make a decision. The inter-caste love story of Jal's brother (Rihan Giri) and Sanisha demands a separate time. However, the love between these two is shown so hastily that the audience cannot feel sympathy for Sanisha's pain. The audience's sympathy for the pregnant Sanisha is suppressed before her pain is revealed. This is the problem when trying to tell the story of a film on the canvas of a 'web series'. The scene of the family voting at Muralidhar's house is dramatic. Moreover, the presence of so many villagers did not make sense. Time has been wasted on this scene. Muralidhar's acting as Jandyaha Kaka is loud. The Newari love is clearly heard in the speech of the character played by Karm. It would have been better if this love was improved a little. Rabindra Jha has not been able to capture the character of the doctor. However, the punching lines of the comedy he does from time to time amuse the audience. Deepak Raj's acting is natural. Keki and Sanisha are solid in their respective roles. It would have been even more enjoyable if Keki's character had been made a little more logical. Keki's character Jal had no room to make strong arguments against her father-in-law, who has been unable to change society despite spending his entire life. Jal's arguments would have created a situation where the father-in-law would have ruthlessly reviewed the politics he has been doing throughout his life. In that case, the father would also be forced to find an answer to the question of whether he will change with time or remain the same. The cinematography and background music in the film are average. The director clearly has a vision for the social issue. However, the film would have been even better if more effort had been put into the way the issue was brought into the story.

विषयमा परिवारमा घनीभूत छलफल हुन्छ । यो छलफलमा बुवा एकातिर, श्रीमती जल एकातिर हुन्छन् । मुरलीधर निर्णय गर्न नसकेर बीचमा च्यापिन्छ । अलिकति पढेलेखेकी जलले आफ्नो विदेश जाने अडान स्पष्ट सँगले राख्छिन् । यसबेला बुवाले जललाई थर्काउँदै ‘महिलाले बढी बोल्न आवश्यक नरहेको’ बताउँछ । जीवनभर वामपन्थी राजनीति गरेका, लैङ्गिक समानताको वकालत गरेका बुवाले जललाई थर्काउँदै आफूभित्र निहित पितृ सत्तालाई बोमिट गरेर निकाल्छन् । मुरलीधरका बुवा जस्ता धेरै वामपन्थी नेताहरू हाम्रै अगाडि छन्, जो बाहिर महिला अधिकारका चर्का कुरा गर्छन्, घरमा महिलालाई ‘वस्तु’ को रूपमा व्यवहार गर्छन् । चलचित्रले ‘समाज बदल्छु’ भन्ने खोक्रा मानिसमाथि व्यङ्ग्य मात्र गरेको छैन, दलितहरूलाई राजनीतिका नाममा, प्रेमका नाममा कसरी प्रयोग गरिन्छ भनेर पनि देखाएको छ । हुँदाहुँदै शिक्षित भनिएका मुरलीधर र जलले समेत दलित युवतीको निरीहताको फाइदा उठाउन खोज्छन् । निर्देशक दीपेन्द्र लामा र दीपकराज गिरीले नेपाली समाजको द्वैध चरित्रलाई खोतल खातल पार्न कोसिस गरेका छन् । चलचित्र जति बलियो मुद्दा उठाएको छ, त्यसको बोझ पटकथाले बोक्न सकेको भने छैन । मुद्दा बलियो भएर मात्र चलचित्र बलियो बन्दैन, त्यो मुद्दालाई कति विश्वासनीय ढङ्गले भनिएको छ भन्ने कुराले चलचित्र बलियो हुने हो । दर्शकले चलचित्रमा घट्ने घटना र पात्रसँगै यात्रा गर्न सक्छन् कि सक्दैनन् ? राम्रो चलचित्रले यस प्रश्नको जवाफ दिन सक्नुपर्छ । चलचित्रको सुरुवाती चरणमा यति धेरै ‘क्रस कटिङ’को प्रयोग गरिएको छ कि दर्शक नै अलमलिन्छन् । आरामले, बिस्तारै, सुस्तरी दृश्यहरूको सम्पादन गरेको भए पनि हुने थियो । धेरै मुद्दाहरू पोको पारेर चलचित्र अन्धाधुन्ध दौडिएको छ । दौडने क्रममा पोको फुस्किएको छ । खासमा समयसँगै बदलिन नसकेका वामपन्थी बा, सहज जीवनयापनको खोजीमा रहेकी जल र निर्णय गर्न नसकिरहेका मुरलीधरबीचको अन्तरसङ्घर्षमा मात्र केन्द्रित भएको भए चलचित्र थप बलियो हुने थियो । जलका भाइ (रिहान गिरी) र सनिशाको अन्तरजातीय प्रेमकथाले अलग्गै समयको माग गर्छ । तर, यी दुईको प्रेमलाई यति हतारमा देखाइएको छ कि सनिशाको पीडामाथि दर्शकले संवेदना महसुस गर्नै सक्दैनन् । गर्भवती बनेकी सनिशामाथि दर्शकको सहानुभूति पलाउन नपाउँदै उनको पीडालाई निमोठिएको छ । ‘बेव सिरिज’को क्यानभासमा चलचित्रको कथा भन्न खोज्दा हुने समस्या नै यही हो । मुरलीधरको घरमा हुने पारिवारिक भोटिङको दृश्य नाटकीय छ । झनै त्यत्रा गाउँलेहरूको उपस्थितिको अर्थै थिएन । यो दृश्यका लागि व्यर्थैमा समय खर्च गरिएको छ । मुरलीधरको जँड्याहा काकाको अभिनय लाउड छ । कार्मले निर्वाह गरेको पात्रको बोलीमा नेवारी लवज प्रस्टै सुनिन्छ । यो लवजलाई अलिकति सुधार गर्न लगाएको भए हुने थियो । रवीन्द्र झाले डाक्टरको पात्र त्यति जम्न सकेका छैनन् । यद्यपि बेलाबेला उनले गर्ने कमेडीको पन्चिङ लाइनहरूले दर्शकलाई रमाइलो गराउँछ । दीपकराजको अभिनय स्वाभाविक छ । केकी र सनिशा आआफ्नो भूमिकामा जमेका छन् । केकीको पात्रलाई अलि तार्किक बनाउन सकेको भए अझैँ स्वादिलो हुने थियो । सिङ्गो जीवन नै लगाए पनि समाज बदल्न नसकेका ससुरामाथि केकीको पात्र जलले दह्रिलो तर्क राख्न सक्ने ठाउँ खाली नै थियो । जलको तर्कले ससुराले जीवनभर गर्ने राजनीतिको निर्मम समीक्षा गर्ने परिस्थितिको सृजना हुने थियो । त्यसो हुँदा समयसँगै बदलिने कि यथास्थितिमै रहने भन्ने प्रश्नको जवाफ खोज्न बा पनि बाध्य हुने थिए । चलचित्रमा सिनेम्याटोग्राफी र ब्याकग्राउण्ड सङ्गीत औसत छ । निर्देशकसँग सामाजिक मुद्दालाई हेर्ने दृष्टिकोण स्पष्ट देखिन्छ । तर, मुद्दालाई कथामा उन्ने तरीकामा थप मिहिनेत गरेको भए चलचित्र अझैँ अब्बल हुने थियो ।

दीपकराज गिरीको चलचित्र भन्नेवित्तिकै दिमागमा आइहाल्ने कुरा हो- हाँस्न पाइन्छ । दर्शकलाई हँसाउँदै गम्भीर सन्देश पनि दिने प्रयास गिरीले अहिलेसम्म गर्दै आएका छन् । उनको नयाँ चलचित्र ‘छ माया छपक्कै २’ अहिले दोस्रो हप्तामा चलिरहेको छ ।

कथा-पटकथामा विभिन्न कमजोरीका बाबजुद ‘छ माया छपक्कै २’ ले निर्मम ढङ्गबाट नेपाली समाजको ढोँगी चरित्रलाई उदाङ्गो पार्ने कोसिस गरेको छ । चलचित्रको विषयवस्तु र प्रस्तुतिमा नयाँपन छ भने केही जबरजस्त ट्वीस्टहरुले गर्दा दर्शक अन्तिमसम्म बाँधिन्छन् ।

चलचित्रमा मुख्य पात्र मुरलीधर (दीपकराज गिरी) पठाओ चलाउँछ । ‘छ माया छपक्कै’ को पहिलो कम्युनिस्ट बाको मार्गदर्शन पछ्याउँदै राजनीतिमा लागेको बिपी धार्मिक आमाको मार्गदर्शन पछ्याउँदै मुरलीधर बनेको छ । आफूभन्दा २० वर्ष कान्छी जल (केकी अधिकारी)सँग विवाह गरेको मुरलीधर घर गृहस्थीमा रमाउन चाहन्छ । तर, समाज बदल्छु भनेर कम्युनिस्ट भएका मुरलीधरका बाको इच्छा छोरालाई राजनीतिमा ल्याउने छ ।

मुरलीधरका बा तिनै हुन्, जो समाज बदल्न हिँडे तर आफ्नै घर बदल्न सकेनन् । आफू नास्तिक बनेर हिँडे, तर घर भने झनझन आस्तिक बनेर गयो । हुँदा हुँदा कम्युनिस्ट बनाउनलाई सारा ऊर्जा र विद्धता खर्च गरेको छोरा बिपी नै अन्त्यमा धार्मिक बन्यो ।

समाज बदल्न हिँडेको बाले घर बदल्न नसकेको फ्रस्टेसन बेलाबेला पोखिरहेका हुन्छन् । बाले मुरलीधरलाई राजनीतिमा फिर्ता ल्याउन चाहन्छन् । आफूले गर्न नसकेको सत्ताभोगको लालसा छोरामाथि थोपर्न चाहन्छन् । आफ्नो अधुरो महत्त्वाकाङ्क्षा मुरलीधरमाथि लाद्न चाहन्छन् । मुरलीधर भने राजनीतिमा फिर्ता हुन चाहँदैन । बरु साधारण र सरल जीवनयापन गरेर बाँच्न चाहन्छ । यही बिन्दुबाट चलचित्रको कथालाई अगाडि बढाइएको छ ।

चलचित्रको एउटा दृश्यमा मुरलीधरले बाको बाटो समातेर राजनीतिमा लाग्ने वा श्रीमतीसँग विदेश गएर सहज जीवनयापन गर्ने भन्ने विषयमा परिवारमा घनीभूत छलफल हुन्छ । यो छलफलमा बुवा एकातिर, श्रीमती जल एकातिर हुन्छन् । मुरलीधर निर्णय गर्न नसकेर बीचमा च्यापिन्छ । अलिकति पढेलेखेकी जलले आफ्नो विदेश जाने अडान स्पष्ट सँगले राख्छिन् । यसबेला बुवाले जललाई थर्काउँदै ‘महिलाले बढी बोल्न आवश्यक नरहेको’ बताउँछ । जीवनभर वामपन्थी राजनीति गरेका, लैङ्गिक समानताको वकालत गरेका बुवाले जललाई थर्काउँदै आफूभित्र निहित पितृ सत्तालाई बोमिट गरेर निकाल्छन् ।

मुरलीधरका बुवा जस्ता धेरै वामपन्थी नेताहरू हाम्रै अगाडि छन्, जो बाहिर महिला अधिकारका चर्का कुरा गर्छन्, घरमा महिलालाई ‘वस्तु’ को रूपमा व्यवहार गर्छन् । चलचित्रले ‘समाज बदल्छु’ भन्ने खोक्रा मानिसमाथि व्यङ्ग्य मात्र गरेको छैन, दलितहरूलाई राजनीतिका नाममा, प्रेमका नाममा कसरी प्रयोग गरिन्छ भनेर पनि देखाएको छ ।

हुँदाहुँदै शिक्षित भनिएका मुरलीधर र जलले समेत दलित युवतीको निरीहताको फाइदा उठाउन खोज्छन् । निर्देशक दीपेन्द्र लामा र दीपकराज गिरीले नेपाली समाजको द्वैध चरित्रलाई खोतल खातल पार्न कोसिस गरेका छन् ।

चलचित्र जति बलियो मुद्दा उठाएको छ, त्यसको बोझ पटकथाले बोक्न सकेको भने छैन । मुद्दा बलियो भएर मात्र चलचित्र बलियो बन्दैन, त्यो मुद्दालाई कति विश्वासनीय ढङ्गले भनिएको छ भन्ने कुराले चलचित्र बलियो हुने हो । दर्शकले चलचित्रमा घट्ने घटना र पात्रसँगै यात्रा गर्न सक्छन् कि सक्दैनन् ? राम्रो चलचित्रले यस प्रश्नको जवाफ दिन सक्नुपर्छ ।

चलचित्रको सुरुवाती चरणमा यति धेरै ‘क्रस कटिङ’को प्रयोग गरिएको छ कि दर्शक नै अलमलिन्छन् । आरामले, बिस्तारै, सुस्तरी दृश्यहरूको सम्पादन गरेको भए पनि हुने थियो । धेरै मुद्दाहरू पोको पारेर चलचित्र अन्धाधुन्ध दौडिएको छ । दौडने क्रममा पोको फुस्किएको छ ।

खासमा समयसँगै बदलिन नसकेका वामपन्थी बा, सहज जीवनयापनको खोजीमा रहेकी जल र निर्णय गर्न नसकिरहेका मुरलीधरबीचको अन्तरसङ्घर्षमा मात्र केन्द्रित भएको भए चलचित्र थप बलियो हुने थियो । जलका भाइ (रिहान गिरी) र सनिशाको अन्तरजातीय प्रेमकथाले अलग्गै समयको माग गर्छ । तर, यी दुईको प्रेमलाई यति हतारमा देखाइएको छ कि सनिशाको पीडामाथि दर्शकले संवेदना महसुस गर्नै सक्दैनन् ।

गर्भवती बनेकी सनिशामाथि दर्शकको सहानुभूति पलाउन नपाउँदै उनको पीडालाई निमोठिएको छ । ‘बेव सिरिज’को क्यानभासमा चलचित्रको कथा भन्न खोज्दा हुने समस्या नै यही हो । मुरलीधरको घरमा हुने पारिवारिक भोटिङको दृश्य नाटकीय छ । झनै त्यत्रा गाउँलेहरूको उपस्थितिको अर्थै थिएन । यो दृश्यका लागि व्यर्थैमा समय खर्च गरिएको छ ।

मुरलीधरको जँड्याहा काकाको अभिनय लाउड छ । कार्मले निर्वाह गरेको पात्रको बोलीमा नेवारी लवज प्रस्टै सुनिन्छ । यो लवजलाई अलिकति सुधार गर्न लगाएको भए हुने थियो । रवीन्द्र झाले डाक्टरको पात्र त्यति जम्न सकेका छैनन् । यद्यपि बेलाबेला उनले गर्ने कमेडीको पन्चिङ लाइनहरूले दर्शकलाई रमाइलो गराउँछ ।

दीपकराजको अभिनय स्वाभाविक छ । केकी र सनिशा आआफ्नो भूमिकामा जमेका छन् । केकीको पात्रलाई अलि तार्किक बनाउन सकेको भए अझैँ स्वादिलो हुने थियो । सिङ्गो जीवन नै लगाए पनि समाज बदल्न नसकेका ससुरामाथि केकीको पात्र जलले दह्रिलो तर्क राख्न सक्ने ठाउँ खाली नै थियो । जलको तर्कले ससुराले जीवनभर गर्ने राजनीतिको निर्मम समीक्षा गर्ने परिस्थितिको सृजना हुने थियो । त्यसो हुँदा समयसँगै बदलिने कि यथास्थितिमै रहने भन्ने प्रश्नको जवाफ खोज्न बा पनि बाध्य हुने थिए । चलचित्रमा सिनेम्याटोग्राफी र ब्याकग्राउण्ड सङ्गीत औसत छ ।

निर्देशकसँग सामाजिक मुद्दालाई हेर्ने दृष्टिकोण स्पष्ट देखिन्छ । तर, मुद्दालाई कथामा उन्ने तरीकामा थप मिहिनेत गरेको भए चलचित्र अझैँ अब्बल हुने थियो ।

When Deepak Raj Giri's movies are mentioned, the first thing that comes to mind is - you can laugh. Giri has been trying to give a serious message while making the audience laugh. His new movie 'Chha Maya Chhapakkai 2' is currently running in its second week. Despite various weaknesses in the story and screenplay, 'Chha Maya Chhapakkai 2' has tried to expose the hypocritical nature of Nepali society in a ruthless manner. The film's theme and presentation are new, and some powerful twists keep the audience hooked until the end. The main character in the movie, Muralidhar (Deepakraj Giri), plays Pathao. BP, who entered politics following the guidance of his first communist father in 'Chha Maya Chhapakkai', has become Muralidhar following the guidance of his religious mother. Muralidhar, who is married to Jal (Keki Adhikari), who is 20 years younger than him, wants to enjoy his home life. However, Muralidhar's father, who became a communist with the intention of changing the society, wants to bring his son into politics. Muralidhar's father is the one who set out to change society but could not change his own family. He set out as an atheist, but his family gradually became believers. His son BP, who spent all his energy and knowledge on becoming a communist, eventually became religious. Bale, who is on a journey to change society, is occasionally expressing his frustration at not being able to change his home. Bale wants to bring Muralidhar back into politics. He wants to impose his own lust for power, which he was unable to do, on his son. He wants to impose his unfulfilled ambitions on Muralidhar. Muralidhar, however, does not want to return to politics. Instead, he wants to live a simple and ordinary life. The story of the film is developed from this point. In one scene of the film, there is a heated discussion in the family about whether Muralidhar should follow his father's path and enter politics or go abroad with his wife and live a comfortable life. In this discussion, the father is on one side, and his wife Jal is on the other. Muralidhar is caught in the middle, unable to decide. Jal, who is a little educated, clearly states her stance on going abroad. At this time, the father rebukes Jal and says that 'women do not need to talk too much'. The father, who has been involved in leftist politics and advocated gender equality all his life, rebukes Jal and brings out the patriarchal power within him. We have many leftist leaders like Muralidhar's father before us, who talk loudly about women's rights outside, but treat women as 'objects' at home. The film not only satirizes the empty people who say 'I will change society', it also shows how Dalits are used in the name of politics, in the name of love. Despite being supposedly educated, Muralidhar and Jal try to take advantage of the Dalit girl's innocence. Directors Dipendra Lama and Deepak Raj Giri have tried to expose the dual nature of Nepali society. The film raises a strong issue, but the script is not able to carry its burden. A film does not become strong just because the issue is strong, it becomes strong because of how believably the issue is told. Can the audience travel with the events and characters in the film or not? A good film should be able to answer this question. So many 'cross-cutting' are used in the initial stages of the film that the audience gets confused. It would have been better if the scenes had been edited slowly, calmly, and smoothly. The film has rushed blindly, covering up many issues. The pacing has been disrupted. In fact, the film would have been stronger if it had focused solely on the internal struggle between the leftist father who has not changed with the times, Jal, who is in search of an easy life, and Muralidhar, who is unable to make a decision. The inter-caste love story of Jal's brother (Rihan Giri) and Sanisha demands a separate time. However, the love between these two is shown so hastily that the audience cannot feel sympathy for Sanisha's pain. The audience's sympathy for the pregnant Sanisha is suppressed before her pain is revealed. This is the problem when trying to tell the story of a film on the canvas of a 'web series'. The scene of the family voting at Muralidhar's house is dramatic. Moreover, the presence of so many villagers did not make sense. Time has been wasted on this scene. Muralidhar's acting as Jandyaha Kaka is loud. The Newari love is clearly heard in the speech of the character played by Karm. It would have been better if this love was improved a little. Rabindra Jha has not been able to capture the character of the doctor. However, the punching lines of the comedy he does from time to time amuse the audience. Deepak Raj's acting is natural. Keki and Sanisha are solid in their respective roles. It would have been even more enjoyable if Keki's character had been made a little more logical. Keki's character Jal had no room to make strong arguments against her father-in-law, who has been unable to change society despite spending his entire life. Jal's arguments would have created a situation where the father-in-law would have ruthlessly reviewed the politics he has been doing throughout his life. In that case, the father would also be forced to find an answer to the question of whether he will change with time or remain the same. The cinematography and background music in the film are average. The director clearly has a vision for the social issue. However, the film would have been even better if more effort had been put into the way the issue was brought into the story.
